annotations.text:
THE ARTBOARDS ARE THE COMPONENT. NOTHING ELSE.

Each frame below contains only what this widget renders: thumbnails. No title, date, channel, description, frame or surface.

The sentences in the notes underneath are the AGENT speaking — rendered by the chat host above the widget, not by us. They sit on the canvas as context so the division of labor is legible, but they are deliberately not drawn inside any artboard: an artboard is a build spec, and anything drawn in one gets built.

AGENT SAYS (host-rendered, above the widget):

"He answers that one pretty directly — his point is that protein restriction is what actually triggers autophagy, not the fasting itself. It's under a minute."

AGENT SAYS (host-rendered, above the widget):

"He's come at this three ways. The first is the 20-second version, the second gets into why insulin matters more than the fasting window itself, and the last is his fuller answer from a carnivore Q&A."

AGENT SAYS (host-rendered, above the widget):

"He talks about fasting a lot — here are six, closest first. The short ones are clips; the three-minute one is where he lays out the whole reasoning."

AGENT SAYS (host-rendered, above the widget):

"All six, if you'd rather just scan them."

THIS COLLAPSES THE VIEW SYSTEM

With no text in the widget, these four stop being different components. They're one strip of thumbnails at different sizes:

1 → full width
2–3 → split to fit
4+ → fixed 172px, scrolls
fullscreen → same tile, wrapped

Still to decide: fold the four ViewModes into one responsive component. It deletes most of carousel.ts and view.ts.

THE ONE THING I KEPT

Duration. It rides on the image rather than around it, so it costs no layout, and the agent can't recite six durations in a sentence.

Say the word and the widget becomes literally just pictures.
Titles aren't deleted, just not drawn — each thumbnail carries its title in aria-label, so screen readers announce the video instead of "link, image". Visually absent, semantically present.
